perspective:
Arthur’s available information:

- He knows himself as Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate.
- He knows Teresa Ortega as a medical-assistant colleague/co-worker; they are collaborating on a community-service project and have worked together before.
- During the project, he observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He feels concerned for her well-being and believes she needs help.
- He offers help. Teresa says it is kind but she thinks she can manage and there is a lot to do. He says self-care matters and offers to help so they can finish faster. Teresa says if he insists, she could use help organizing medical supplies. He agrees, and they start.
- He believes Teresa is hesitant because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathy and wants to reassure her that accepting help does not undermine her abilities.
- He tells Teresa he admires her wish to handle things herself, but accepting help does not mean she is not capable. Teresa says she appreciates it but wants to show she can do it by herself. He says teamwork can be more effective and it is not about proving anything. Teresa agrees she needs reminding of that. He says they are in it together and he supports her.
- He later believes Teresa is still struggling and feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results. He wants another way to support her without making her feel inadequate.
- He tells Teresa he sees things are still tough and she is doing a great job. Teresa says it has been a busy day and she feels behind. He suggests working together on tasks to share the load. Teresa agrees. He says they will tackle it as a team.
- He believes working together will ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He feels hopeful and intends to fully commit to the collaborative approach.
- He tells Teresa he is hopeful collaboration will make things easier. Teresa says it already feels less overwhelming. He says he will handle inventory while she manages patient records, with regular check-ins. Teresa agrees. He says they will make it a productive day.
- He believes their collaboration has strengthened their professional relationship. He feels satisfied with the outcome and intends to maintain the collaborative approach in future projects.
- He tells Teresa their teamwork paid off and they accomplished more together. He suggests continuing the collaborative approach in future projects. Teresa agrees it is a fantastic idea and says they are more efficient and effective as a team. He says he looks forward to their next project. Teresa thanks him for being supportive.
